hunks.baseline: The next moment, a clear laugh flowed between the officer’s lips. It was filled with genuine amusement, not something she had forced.

hunks.sol: “Child. I am merely a lowly servant who moves according to orders. No one can presume to fathom that person’s will.”

hunks.baseline: Everyone present knew whom those two syllables referred to.
hunks.sol: Everyone present knew whom those two words referred to.

hunks.baseline: Crack.

hunks.sol: “I’ve heard that a crazed old monster lives on Mount Jiuhua. Fire King Jeok Cheongang, you are correct. It is indeed that person. The greatest and noblest of all…”

hunks.baseline: “You’re talking about a fucking bastard who wouldn’t be worth the satisfaction of burning alive. How dare you wag that wicked tongue before this old man?”
hunks.sol: “You mean a fucking bastard who wouldn’t be worth the satisfaction of burning alive. How dare you wag that wicked tongue before this old man?”

hunks.sol: A brief silence followed Jeok Cheongang’s words, which carried a cold flame.

hunks.baseline: Then the officer’s tightly closed lips slowly opened, and a low voice flowed out.
hunks.sol: Then the officer’s tightly closed lips slowly parted, and a subdued voice flowed out.

hunks.baseline: “You should choose your words more carefully if you want to hold on to your stubborn life a little longer.”
hunks.sol: “You’d best choose your words more carefully if you wish to cling to that stubborn life of yours a little longer.”

hunks.baseline: Jeok Cheongang snorted and asked me,

hunks.sol: “Then how would you feel about this old man adding a bitch instead of a bastard to his kill list?”

hunks.baseline: And rather than be thrown from its back, I would end this insane struggle even if I had to smash the tiger’s skull to do it.
hunks.sol: And rather than let it throw me off, I would end its mad struggle even if I had to smash its skull to do it.

hunks.baseline: I exhaled the breath I had been holding, then leaned close to the military officer. Looking through the soul-less eyes at some distant place, I spoke.
hunks.sol: I exhaled the breath I had been holding and leaned close to the military officer. I stared past his soulless eyes at someone far away.

hunks.baseline: “When we meet again… you will die.”
hunks.sol: “When we meet again… you’re going to die.”

hunks.baseline: The head slowly turned. Its unfocused, milky eyes looked over everyone in the room one by one.
hunks.sol: His head slowly turned. His unfocused, milky eyes swept over everyone in the room one by one.

hunks.baseline: “You should stop this futile killing. Blades eventually turn back on the person wielding them.”
hunks.sol: “You should put an end to this futile killing. A blade always turns back on its wielder in the end.”

hunks.baseline: His tone and voice were polite, clearly conscious of the eyes around him. But hidden within them was a blade only a handful of people could detect.
hunks.sol: His voice and tone were polite, mindful of the others around him. But hidden within them was a blade only a handful of people could detect.

hunks.baseline: That was the true nature of the greatest assassin in history—a supreme martial artist known as the Slaughter Saint, who had walked nothing but blood-soaked paths.
hunks.sol: It was the true face of the greatest assassin of all time—the supreme martial artist known as the Slaughter Saint, who had walked a path stained with nothing but blood.

hunks.baseline: “…What an unusual child. Unusual enough to make me curious about this person called the Divine Physician.”
hunks.sol: “…What an unusual child. Unusual enough to make me curious about this Divine Physician.”

hunks.sol: She might have known his public identity as the Divine Physician’s Disciple, but the connection between the Slaughter Saint who had vanished forty years ago and a young medical apprentice was far too tenuous.
